memos.risk:
Risk view on PACK: refuse.

The brief is mixed in ways that matter. The coin is up 133% over 30 minutes and has a 26% drawdown from its high, and recent volume is large. But the curve shows a 49% bundle share, a launch bot present, and a sell-to-buy ratio of 0.91 in the first two minutes after graduation. Those are classic signs of coordinated early supply, not organic demand. Net flow over the last 15 minutes is only +21 SOL against 808 SOL of buying, so the book is churning hard with thin conviction.

Pool depth of 133 SOL means a $20 ticket is roughly 0.1% of the pool, but the 1.4-5.1% round-trip cost plus a sell-side that is already heavy makes exit slippage the real danger.

Sizing if the desk overrides: $5, not $20. Stop at 20%, since the coin already shows a 26% drawdown and a fast move down is plausible. Hold 15 minutes at most.

I would refuse any size on this coin. The base rates favor skipping, and the bundling plus launch-bot pattern is a reason to pass, not a reason to trade smaller.

Case for buying PACK now is thin, and I'd lean toward skipping.

What's in its favor: the coin is alive at 30 minutes, classed ORGANIC with no airdrop dump, and it has real volume: about $191k over 15 minutes with 2,553 buyers and 1,685 sellers. The 15-minute net flow is slightly positive (+21 SOL), and 30-minute return is +133%. The top-3 curve holder share is low (4.2%) and the top-5 buyer share at graduation was only 6.5%.

What argues against it: the sell-to-buy ratio right after graduation was 0.91 and the 15-minute sells ($787k worth of SOL) nearly match buys, so holders are cycling out as fast as they come in. It is already 26% off its 30-minute high. Nearly half the curve buying (49%) came from bundled wallets, and a launch bot was present. Graduation took 500 seconds. Our 30-60 minute window is exactly where the base rates say these coins usually fade, and the ~1.4-5.1% round-trip cost plus a 30-second fill delay eat into any small bounce.

No strong honest case for real demand persisting 30-60 minutes out. I'd skip.
